thesisInOneSentence: Performers replace the O(n^2) softmax attention matrix with a random-feature kernel trick, then re-associate (phi(Q) phi(K)^T) V into phi(Q) (phi(K)^T V), turning attention into linear time without changing what the model can express.
audience: Working ML engineers who already know what a Transformer is, have probably tweeted about quadratic attention, and want the actual trick in 3 minutes — not a graduate seminar.
hook: Attention is O(n^2). That wall is why your context window is 8k instead of 8 million. Performers tear it down with a kernel trick from 2007.

teaser.openingLine: Attention is O(n squared). Double the tokens, quadruple the compute. That is the wall every long-context model slams into.
teaser.stakes: If you can rewrite that quadratic into a linear pass — without breaking softmax — you unlock million-token Transformers on a single GPU.
teaser.openLoop: How do you replace softmax(QK^T) — a non-linear, dense L by L matrix — with something that scales linearly? Spoiler: you do not compute it at all.
teaser.visualConcept: Cold open: bold sans-serif 'O(n^2)' fills the screen, pulses red. Cut to a bar chart of memory blowing up. Quick zoom on the paper's title. Title card 'PERFORMERS — attention, but linear' lands as the LAST beat.

narrativeArc.name: Teaser
narrativeArc.purpose: Cold-open hook in Fireship cadence. Beats: (1) 'Attention is O(n^2)' punch. (2) Stakes: this is THE bottleneck. (3) Tease: a 2007 kernel trick fixes it. (4) Open-loop question: 'how do you skip the L by L matrix entirely?' (5) Title card 'Performers — attention, but linear' as payoff. No equations on screen. Chunky type, fast cuts.

narrativeArc.name: The O(n^2) wall
narrativeArc.purpose: Set the bottleneck precisely. Show standard attention: softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d)) V. Highlight the L x L matrix A. State the cost: O(L^2 d) compute, O(L^2) memory. Drop a concrete number ('a 16k context blows past 1 GB just for ONE attention matrix'). Land the pain: 'this is why your context window is small.' Quick paperPage zoom on Equation 1.

narrativeArc.name: The kernel trick
narrativeArc.purpose: The big idea. Reframe softmax(q^T k) as a kernel K(q,k). Any kernel can be written as K(x,y) = E[phi(x)^T phi(y)] for some random feature map phi. So the L x L matrix A is approximated by phi(Q) phi(K)^T — a product of two L x r matrices. Beat sequence: kernel definition → 'wait you can do that?' moment → caveat (negative features explode, they fix it with positive random features exp(omega^T x - ||x||^2/2)). Use equationStep to reveal eq-003 then eq-007. One paperPage spotlight on Lemma 1.

narrativeArc.name: The linear-time rewrite
narrativeArc.purpose: The punchline. Show (phi(Q) phi(K)^T) V — still L^2 if you compute the middle. Then re-associate: phi(Q) (phi(K)^T V). The middle term is now r x d. Total cost: O(L r d) — LINEAR in L. This is one Manim beat: associativity arrows collapsing the parens. Drop the benchmark: 'forward pass goes from 8k tokens choking to 64k tokens fine on the same GPU.' Quick paperPage zoom on Figure 3.

narrativeArc.name: The fine print
narrativeArc.purpose: Caveats and close. One breath each: (1) it's an unbiased approximation, not exact. (2) FAVOR+ uses ORTHOGONAL random features for lower variance — one-line callout. (3) Drop-in compatible with pretrained Transformers via small finetune. Close with arxiv ID + GitHub. Title card with paper title and 2009.14794.

questionsToAnswerOnScreen: Can you rewrite softmax as a kernel?
What is phi and where does it come from?
Why does moving the parentheses make it linear?
Is it actually equal, or just an approximation?
thingsToCutOrSkip: Unbiasedness proofs (Lemmas 2-4, Theorems 1-4) — mention 'provably unbiased' in one breath, do not derive.
All trigonometric random feature MSE comparison — say 'sin/cos blows up, exp does not' and move on.
The orthogonality construction (Gram-Schmidt details, ORF theory) — one sentence callout: 'orthogonal features cut variance further'.
Unidirectional / causal prefix-sum trick (Appendix B.1) — do not mention; it adds complexity for no payoff in 3 min.
Protein modeling experiments and TrEMBL ablations — out of scope.
Generalized kernel choices (ReLU features, etc.) — skip.
All of Sections 3 and 4.4-4.7 — pure theory and ablations.
The regularized softmax-kernel SMREG — skip entirely.
Comparisons to Reformer / Linformer / Longformer beyond a single benchmark glance.
The 'redrawing random features periodically' training detail — too in-the-weeds.

derivationsToBuild.openingQuestion: If A = phi(Q) phi(K)^T, why is computing A V still O(L^2)? And how does one parenthesis change everything?
stepsToShow: Show A V written as (phi(Q) phi(K)^T) V — middle product is L x L, still quadratic.
Now phi(K)^T V is r x d — tiny, independent of L.
Final multiply phi(Q) by (r x d) is O(L r d) — linear in L.
Side-by-side dimension callouts: nowhere does L x L appear.

derivationsToBuild.concept: softmax as a kernel via positive random features (compressed)
derivationsToBuild.openingQuestion: Can softmax(q^T k) really be written as phi(q)^T phi(k)?
stepsToShow: Identity: exp(x^T y) = E_omega [ exp(omega^T x - ||x||^2 / 2) * exp(omega^T y - ||y||^2 / 2) ] for omega ~ N(0, I).
Read off phi(x) = exp(omega^T x - ||x||^2 / 2) — positive, well-behaved.
Stack m samples → phi: R^d → R^m, plug into Equation 4.

metaphors.concept: the kernel trick replacing the L x L matrix
metaphors.metaphor: It is like replacing a giant lookup table with a hash function. Instead of materializing every (query, key) score, you hand each token a 'fingerprint' phi, and dot products of fingerprints reproduce the scores you would have computed.
metaphors.whenToDeploy: Beat 1 of act-2, right before showing eq-003. One sentence. Drop and move on.

metaphors.metaphor: Same equation, different parentheses, billion-times-cheaper compute. Like factoring a slow loop into matmul.
metaphors.whenToDeploy: Beat 1 of act-3, immediately before the Manim associativity clip.

narrativeAngles: The 'one weird trick' framing: a 2007 kernel-method paper, applied to 2017 Transformers, breaks the O(n^2) wall in 2020.
Frame it as engineering plumbing, not theory: 'the math is unchanged, only the order of operations changes.' This is what makes it Fireship-shaped.
Implicit competitive frame: while everyone else (Reformer, Longformer, Linformer) sparsifies or low-ranks attention, Performers keep softmax full-rank and just refuse to materialize the matrix.
criticisms: The paper buries the punchline (Equation 4 + Figure 1) under a section of kernel preliminaries. We MUST lead with the rewrite and backfill the kernel justification — invert the paper's order.

The paper conflates 'FAVOR+' (positive + orthogonal random features + algorithm) with the much simpler core trick (kernel feature map + associativity). For 3 minutes, only the core trick matters; FAVOR+ is a one-line callout.
Figure 1 in the paper is fine but typographically dense — re-render the associativity collapse cleanly in Manim with bold dim labels (L x r), (r x d), no axes, no clutter.

Lemma 1's identity exp(x^T y) = E[exp(omega^T x - ||x||^2/2) * exp(omega^T y - ||y||^2/2)] is non-obvious and the paper just states it. We do NOT derive — we present it as a fact and move on, otherwise we blow the time budget.
